notesStmt.note: This manuscript was likely composed in late 1889 or early 1890.
This manuscript contains an early draft of "Osceola," a poem first published in Munyon's Illustrated World in April 1890. It was then included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

lg.head: Osceola

l.add: When The prisoner's His hour of for death had come

lg.l: He ‸slowly rose ‸raised himself from his bed on the floor
He drew his leggings on, his war-dress and leggings, shirt
W Girdled the belt around his waist

Call'd for the red vermilion pain (his slooking glass
was held before him)

Painted one half his face and neck, his
wrists and back-hands

Placed Put his scalp-knife in the belt
then, lying resting

Rose, again, smiled, gave ‸in silence his extended kindly hand to
each and all

Then sank, to the floor, tightly grasp'd
the tomahawk handle
Turn'd his eyes on his wife and little children —the last,

(And here a line in memory
of his na death)
